name: Germany
sources: No per-nation sourcing note existed when this nation was first entered in init.rs; the table header recorded only "Transcribed-not-invented: approximate 1990 historical starting conditions".
Figures below are transcribed unchanged from that table. Their origin was not documented at the time and is a known gap in provenance.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.2282%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series DEU (Germany): 77,858,685 in 1984 to 78,751,283 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 22 were held and are listed below with their citations; 26 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, comp_risc_superscalar, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_conjugate_vaccine, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture.

COLLISION RESOLVED. Two authoring boards ruled the same cell for this nation and disagreed. The tie-break is uniform across the whole roster and is not a preference between authors: the cell belongs to the board that owns the technology's domain in the registry, which for every non-core id is also its id prefix, and which both cross-domain authors published as their own deferral. core_packet_internetworking -> NOT HELD (semiconductors-computing said held, telecom-space said not held; resolved to the board that owns the Communications domain, telecom-space).

SECOND AUTHORING PASS, 2026-08-31, USE-SIDE ONLY. The first pass was correctly instructed to rule NOT HELD when unsure, and produced a defensible but ragged board: the convergence channel was reading that transcription's INCOMPLETENESS as this nation's IGNORANCE, and paying it to catch up to things it already had. A second pass therefore re-ruled the 31 USE-SIDE nodes against an explicit standard published before any nation was looked at, each limb written separately into every source string. LIMB A: a citable fact putting the technology in general commercial or public service across the OECD on or before 31 December 1989, asserted once per technology and identical for every nation. LIMB B: the nation is in the Advanced Set - 1990 OECD member AND World Bank high-income in the 1990 groupings AND one of the 29 authored majors: australia canada france germany italy japan netherlands spain sweden switzerland uk usa. LIMB C: a performed and RECORDED search for a named fact placing the nation outside that deployment; a silent limb C is a failed limb C. Where limb A failed for a technology the board said so and fell back to the first pass's named-artefact bar rather than granting on the class claim - which is why several second-pass refusals contradict the brief's own opening cut. THE SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE BAR IS UNCHANGED: producing a jet engine is still producing a jet engine, and not one of the 17 sovereignty-side ids was added, removed or re-reasoned by this pass. THE PASS IS ADDITIONS-ONLY - no first-pass grant was removed or weakened - and it was authored blind of model output, with the simulation never run and no CAGR, gap or instrument reading consulted. ADDED BY THE SECOND PASS FOR THIS NATION, 3 cells: bio_monoclonal_antibody (health and agriculture board), bio_recombinant_pharma (health and agriculture board), core_combined_cycle_turbine (energy and transport board). The refused list above has been reduced by exactly those ids and by nothing else; every other first-pass refusal stands untouched, and each new grant carries its own citation below.

granted.source: Route (a) production. Siemens began megabit-chip production at Regensburg in early 1987 using Toshiba know-how, the 1-Mbit part requiring 1.2-micron design rules, and started series production of the 4-Mbit DRAM in late 1989 - Siemens corporate history, '4-megabit DRAM chip'; Heinz Nixdorf MuseumsForum blog, 'Mythos Megabit'; Computerwoche, 'Siemens hinkt mit Megachip hinterher'. Corroboration for use: IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 8.22 PCs per 100.

Sigri Elektrographit produced carbon fibre as Sigrafil at Meitingen - the line that became SGL Carbon's on the 1992 Sigri / Great Lakes merger - and MBB cured carbon fibre into primary structure: the A310-300's CFRP vertical stabiliser, on an aircraft that first flew on 8 July 1985 and entered airline service in 1986. WEAKER LEG STATED: the fibre line is the less certain of the two. BASF owned the Celion carbon-fibre business from 1985 but that plant was in the United States, so it is a corporate and not a territorial fact and is not relied on.

LIMB A: as re-ruled in this node's note, the class claim FAILS - combined-cycle plant was not in general commercial service across the OECD on 31 December 1989 - so this cell is granted on the first pass's named-artefact bar and not on the class. LIMB B: Germany is in the Advanced Set (OECD member on 1 January 1990, high-income in the World Bank 1990 groupings, and one of the 29 authored majors); admitted on the FRG basis per the owner's standing ruling, and this grant is NOT discounted for the GDR - the station cited is in Lower Saxony, in the western Laender. EVIDENCE E2, a named artefact in the nation, dated: Kraftwerk Landesbergen on the Weser in Lower Saxony. Block IV, described by the German-language record as 'ein Gas-und-Dampf-Kombiblock', was commissioned in 1973 at a rated 510 MW - 60 MW from the gas turbine and 450 MW from the steam turbine - on a site that had been Germany's first large natural-gas power station in 1962. It remained in service until Statkraft decided in March 2013 to shut the gas plant down and keep the gas turbine on standby reserve, so the block was generating on 1 January 1990. Source: de.wikipedia, 'Kraftwerk Landesbergen'; Statkraft, 'Landesbergen Gaskraftwerk'. LIMB C SEARCHED: no named, citable fact was found placing Germany outside combined-cycle operation, and the contrary evidence is that Germany ran the technology continuously from 1973. DISCLOSED LIMIT: a 60 MW gas turbine ahead of a 450 MW steam turbine is a topping arrangement rather than the balanced modern CCGT that the registry's F-class comment has in mind, and this grant rests on the German source's own classification of Block IV as a Gas-und-Dampf-Kombiblock. A reader who requires a balanced combined cycle should reverse this cell - in which case the pre-1990 OECD combined-cycle fleet is the USA and Japan alone, which would be a still more restrictive reading than the one taken here.

The European Molecular Biology Laboratory at Heidelberg, of which the Federal Republic was a founding member state, was building and running its own fluorescent DNA sequencing apparatus under Wilhelm Ansorge in the mid-1980s; Boehringer Mannheim was one of the world's principal commercial suppliers of molecular-biology enzymes. Germany had both the laboratories and the reagent supply for PCR as routine method by 1989.
World Bank IT.CMP.PCMP.P2 1990 = 8.22 PCs per 100, 3.4x the World value of 2.45.
Oracle established a German subsidiary within three years of 1982 (Oracle corporate histories, as above). Germany also holds comp_microprocessor at 8.22 PCs per 100.

R3: the Deutsche Bundespost's C-Netz analogue cellular network was inaugurated in 1985 on Siemens' C450 standard and operated to 2000. World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 272,609 German mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990. Siemens' own EWSD digital exchange system had been in production since 1975.

DFS Kopernikus 1, the German national communications satellite, was launched on 5 June 1989 and built for the Deutsche Bundespost by the GESAT consortium: MBB/ERNO as flight-segment prime contractor, Siemens as overall prime, ANT Nachrichtentechnik supplying the payload. German prime contractor, German payload, flown seven months before the start date.

The Deutsche Bundespost's C-Netz analogue cellular network was inaugurated in 1985 on Siemens' C450 standard and ran until 2000 (in some areas 2001). World Bank WDI IT.CEL.SETS records 272,609 German mobile cellular subscriptions in 1990.

The Pellworm island photovoltaic plant in North Frisia - roughly 300 kW, commissioned 1983 and the largest photovoltaic installation in Europe when built, feeding the island supply; the Kobern-Gondorf plant on the Mosel followed in 1988. NOTE ON THE DATE HAZARD: the registry's cited exemplar for this node is Germany's 1,000 Roofs programme, which launched IN 1990 and is therefore after the start date. The grant does not rest on it. It rests on the West German installations that were already generating in the 1980s, which is the half of the registry comment that is safely pre-1990 ('the process was in volume production through the 1980s').

Siemens delivered the first German 1 Mb DRAM in 1987 under the Megaproject with Philips and carried the line into the 4 Mb generation, at Regensburg and Munich-Perlach. MODERATE: the 1987 1 Mb date is firm; 4 Mb volume production as at 1 January 1990 is the softer leg.

MBB's CFRP vertical stabiliser for the A310-300 - the first carbon-fibre primary structure on a civil airliner - on an aircraft that first flew on 8 July 1985 and entered airline service in 1986, followed by the A320's CFRP fin, in service from March 1988.

KUKA of Augsburg built the FAMULUS in 1973, the first six-axis electromechanically driven industrial robot, and was in series production of arms and controllers through the 1980s, with Reis and Cloos beside it. This roster's Germany is the unified state, but the grant rests on West German industry alone and does not need the GDR programme.

Vacuumschmelze at Hanau produced sintered NdFeB as VACODYM into German motor and instrument manufacture. MODERATE on the exact production start year, which I have not pinned; the producer and the product line are firm.

LIMB A as in the technology note. LIMB B: Advanced Set. CLASS E2: Danne T, Grueters A, Schnabel K, Burger W et al., 'Long-term monitoring of treatment with recombinant human growth hormone by serial determinations of type III procollagen-related antigens in serum', Pediatric Research 1988;23(2):167-71 (PMID 3353159), Free University Children's Clinic, Klinikum Charlottenburg, West Berlin. The word that carries the cell is LONG-TERM: by February 1988 a Berlin university children's clinic was not starting recombinant hGH but monitoring an established course of it. Corroborated by Division of Pediatric Nephrology, University Children's Hospital, Heidelberg, on recombinant hGH in uraemic growth failure in the same window (Kidney International 1988, PMID 3352160). LIMB C SEARCHED AND ONE CANDIDATE SPECIFICALLY CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: Hoechst's recombinant human insulin plant at Frankfurt was held up for years by the Hessen authorities, but that is a defeater for German PRODUCTION and this node is use-side, where the test is whether the drug was administered here. EAST GERMANY: per the Advanced Set ruling, Germany is admitted on the FRG basis and this grant is not discounted for the GDR; the Berlin and Heidelberg clinics are in the western Laender.

WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 coverage, Germany, 1990: 80% — exactly at the WHO Universal Childhood Immunization 1990 target, and the lowest figure in Western Europe. The reason is documented and specific: the German general recommendation for pertussis vaccination was withdrawn in the mid-1970s over adverse-event concerns and was not reinstated until the early 1990s, which depressed the third-dose DTP figure while diphtheria and tetanus coverage remained high. Series: WUENIC DTP3 ('Germany,DEU,1990,80'); the roster's Germany carries population 79.0m, i.e. the combined German state, which is the entity the DEU series names. THRESHOLD CELL — flips out on any threshold above 80.

Grant rests on the MRI-and-conventional-CT half. Siemens Medical Systems at Erlangen built both: the SOMATOM computed-tomography series from the mid-1970s and the MAGNETOM magnetic-resonance system from the mid-1980s. The SOMATOM Plus-S helical scanner that this node's own comment dates the entry from was also a Siemens machine, and it shipped in 1990 — after the start date, which is precisely why the grant does not rest on it.

NAMED-ARTEFACT BAR (limb A withdrawn for this node - see technology note), CLASS E2: Bluemke M, Kirste G, Wanner G, Wilms H et al., 'Single center randomized trial using ATG v OKT3 treatment in steroid resistant rejection crises after kidney transplantation', Transplantation Proceedings 1989;21(1 Pt 2):1747 (PMID 2652571), Department of Surgery, University Hospital Freiburg im Breisgau. A single centre with enough steroid-resistant rejection crises to randomise between two rescue agents is a unit in which muromonab-CD3 is stocked and given. Corroborated by a second named German centre in the same window, Medizinische Klinik III, Universitaet Muenchen, Klinikum Grosshadern, in the 1986-89 OKT3 title literature. LIMB C SEARCHED: nothing found. Germany admitted on the FRG basis per the Advanced Set ruling; both centres are in the western Laender.

Wilhelm Ansorge's group at the European Molecular Biology Laboratory in Heidelberg built and published an automated fluorescent DNA sequencer in the mid-1980s; the design was licensed to Pharmacia-LKB and sold as the A.L.F. CAVEAT STATED IN THE OPEN: EMBL is an intergovernmental laboratory sited in Heidelberg, of which the Federal Republic was a founding member state. The grant rests on the machine having been built and run on German soil, not on German ownership of it, and a reader is entitled to reject it on exactly that ground.

DAKOSY, Hamburg, created in 1982: the first port community system in Europe, exchanging cargo and customs data across the Hamburg port community. Piernext (Port de Barcelona), 'The fourth wave of Port Community Systems' ('Hamburg (Dakosy, 1982)').

The Wurzburg-Fulda section of the purpose-built Hannover-Wurzburg Schnellfahrstrecke was put into operation on 29 May 1988 and worked by Deutsche Bundesbahn InterCity trains; 160 InterCity coaches were made pressure-tight during 1988 and 1989 to lift the initial 160 km/h tunnel restriction on a line designed for 200 km/h. de.wikipedia, 'Schnellfahrstrecke Hannover-Wurzburg'. DISCLOSED LIMIT: this is a high-speed LINE in scheduled service, not a high-speed SERVICE - ICE operation over the completed line began only in June 1991. Under a 'dedicated high-speed service' standard this cell flips to not held.

West Germany's Grossfeuerungsanlagen-Verordnung (13. BImSchV) of 1983, enacted in response to Waldsterben, forced retrofit FGD across the large-combustion fleet, and the German series shows a rapid increase in retrofit FGD through the 1980s (Nature Communications 11 (2020), 'Diffusion of flue gas desulfurization...', which attributes the German 1980s retrofit wave to the comprehensive 1983 regulation). The tree's own entry comment names West Germany as its other 1980s deployment (spheres-sim/src/tech/agriculture.rs:167-172).
